items.title: John Levy interviewed by Monk Rowe, Majesty of the Seas, May 31, 1995
items.q: Raymond Walters was the first pianist with us, and he worked with us maybe in Chicago for maybe about two or three months.

ctx.x: Louis Armstrong, Dizzy, you name it. Especially trumpet players. He had Red Allen and Higginbotham and that group, the Dixieland groups. He had control over all of these different groups — Billie Holiday and you name it — Dinah Washington, he had all of these people. And so I got to know him first by just sending, make sure I sent that commission into him. So he sort of got a respect for me as a business person. So in 1944

we got a job to go to 52nd Street and open in the Onyx Club. And in those days they gave you a long term deal, so the deal was for six months. And Jimmy Jones, I’m sort of ahead of myself, because actually Jimmy Jones joined the group — Raymond Walters was the first pianist with us, and he worked with us maybe in Chicago for maybe about two or three months. And then Jimmy Jones and I had been friends, I knew him as a player and I recommended that he come on with us. And that’s how the real Stuff Smith Trio got…

items.title: John Levy — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: Raymond Walters was a great piano piano. I knew him, but I had never worked with him before. Then there was Stuff. That was the trio.

ctx.x: The president of the black musicians’ union called me one day. He said, “You know Stuff Smith?” I said, “Yeah, I know of him, but I don’t know him personally. I know who he is.” He said, “There’s an offer for him to come into Chicago to work at a club, but I won’t allow him to work at any club here unless somebody is working with him who’s going to take care of business,” he said, “because he is too flighty and he’s liable to do anything – not pay the guys and cause trouble. I won’t allow him to work. But if…

Raymond Walters was the piano player that – Harry Gray was the name of the president of the union – that Harry had put together with – Raymond Walters was a great piano piano. I knew him, but I had never worked with him before. Then there was Stuff. That was the trio. But as we worked along, Raymond decided to go with another group called Burns Campbell. He was a local group too, a guitar player, Burns Campbell. They went together. They got together, so he left, and I brought in Jimmy Jones to take his place,…
When you arrived on 52nd Street – and I guess this is your first time?
